ownership_reason: Only the gold compares an element with the elements already appended; hops 1-4 hold the whole list, copy it, clear it or collect it into a set, and never compare two elements, and the list that the gold refills is the caller's own list, which the facade wraps (the facade calls the protected SetUniqueList constructor itself because no host can reach it, exactly as the original body ends). The gold promises to append each element of the collection that the list does not already contain; after 1 and 2 the list contains the second, distinct Integer 1, so appending it violates that contract. The convention that an equal element, not only the same instance, is already contained is pinned outside the gold: SetUniqueList.addAll adds only elements that are not already in the list and ignores duplicates of the specified collection (SetUniqueListTest testAddAll adds two distinct new Integer(1) instances and expects one); SetUniqueList.add tests set.contains; AbstractLinkedList.isEqualValue (value1 == value2 || (value1 == null ? false : value1.equals(value2))) and AbstractHashedMap.isEqualKey (key1 == key2 || key1.equals(key2)) use the same identity-or-equals idiom; the facade's javadoc says duplicates are removed, first indexed one kept. A hop can absorb the repeats only by implementing the removal a second time (CollectionUtils.filter with UniquePredicate, or a LinkedHashSet copy at hop 4, which is then no longer the copy of the list that hop 4's javadoc describes); a HashSet copy at hop 4 passes the suite but loses the list order (setUniqueList of ["b", "a"] would give [a, b]).
